resources.title: Do I need to take a test?

intro: Washington instruction permits start at 15, and the knowledge test has 40 multiple-choice questions — you need 32 correct. Our Washington bank is built from the official Washington State Driver Guide.

testTypes.name: Personal driver license
testTypes.description: The written multiple-choice knowledge test for a Washington personal driver license.

notes: The knowledge test is a written multiple-choice test. You must get 32 out of 40 correct to pass.
A passing score is good for 2 years. If you do not pass, there may be a waiting period before you can retest.

source.title: Do I need to take a test? — Washington State Department of Licensing

mockPresets.label: Full 40-question mock
mockPresets.description: Official format: 40 multiple-choice questions. Pass with 32 correct.

commonMistakes.text: Holding your phone at a red light. Washington's rule is that you cannot hold any electronic device while driving.
Stopping too close to the tracks. When you stop for a train, stay between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail.
Assuming ABS shortens stopping distance. It helps you steer while braking — it does not make you stop sooner.

faq.q: How many questions are on the Washington knowledge test?
faq.a: 40 multiple-choice questions. You need 32 correct to pass, and a passing score is good for 2 years.

faq.q: How old do I need to be for a Washington instruction permit?
faq.a: You can apply as early as 15. Without a driver training course, you can take the knowledge exam after you turn 15½.

faq.q: How many supervised hours do teens need in Washington?
faq.a: At least 40 hours of day driving and 10 hours of night driving with a licensed driver, plus holding the permit for at least 6 months.

questions.question: How old must you be to apply for an instruction permit in Washington?
questions.explanation: Washington's driver guide says you can apply for your instruction permit as early as age 15.

questions.question: If you are not enrolled in a driver training course, when can you take the Washington knowledge exam?
questions.explanation: The guide says you can take the knowledge exam after you turn 15½.

questions.question: How long is a Washington instruction permit valid?
questions.explanation: A Washington instruction permit is valid for 1 year and can be renewed for a fee.

questions.question: How long does a passing Washington knowledge exam score remain valid?
questions.explanation: Your knowledge exam score is only valid for 2 years.

questions.question: A 16- or 17-year-old in Washington must hold an instruction permit for at least how long before getting a license?
questions.explanation: Applicants aged 16 or 17 must have had their instruction permit for at least 6 months.

questions.question: How much supervised driving must a 16- or 17-year-old complete before getting a Washington license?
options: At least 20 hours, any time of day
At least 30 hours of day driving and 5 hours of night driving
At least 40 hours of day driving and 10 hours of night driving
At least 60 hours of day driving and 20 hours of night driving
questions.correctAnswer: At least 40 hours of day driving and 10 hours of night driving
questions.explanation: Teen applicants must complete at least 40 hours of day driving and 10 hours of night driving with a licensed driver.

questions.question: During the first phase of a Washington intermediate license, which passengers are allowed?
options: No passengers under age 20 except immediate family members
Any passengers if a parent approves
No passengers at all, including family
questions.correctAnswer: No passengers under age 20 except immediate family members
questions.explanation: In the first phase, intermediate drivers may carry no passengers under age 20 except immediate family members.
questions.sourceSection: 1.8: Getting a personal driver license — Intermediate driver license

questions.question: When may a Washington intermediate license holder NOT drive unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least 25?
questions.explanation: Intermediate drivers may not drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least age 25.
questions.sourceSection: 1.8: Getting a personal driver license — Intermediate driver license

questions.question: In the second phase of a Washington intermediate license, how many passengers under age 20 (not immediate family) may ride with you?
questions.explanation: In the second phase, intermediate drivers may carry no more than 3 passengers under age 20, except immediate family members.
questions.sourceSection: 1.8: Getting a personal driver license — Intermediate driver license

questions.question: In Washington, if your license has been expired for 8 or more years, what must you do?
options: Retake the knowledge and skills tests
questions.correctAnswer: Retake the knowledge and skills tests
questions.explanation: If your license is 8 or more years expired, you'll need to retake the skills and knowledge test.

questions.question: For a Washington driver age 21 or older, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered a DUI?
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of .08% or higher is considered a DUI.

questions.question: Washington drivers under 21 face DUI-type consequences at what BAC?
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 face the same potential consequences at a BAC of 0.02%.

questions.question: For a Washington driver age 21 or older, how much active THC in the blood is considered a DUI?
questions.explanation: Having more than 5 nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood is considered a DUI for drivers 21 and older.

questions.question: For Washington drivers under 21, how much active THC in the blood can lead to DUI consequences?
options: Anything more than 0 nanograms per milliliter
Only amounts over the adult limit
questions.correctAnswer: Anything more than 0 nanograms per milliliter
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 face consequences for anything more than 0 nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood.

questions.question: What does Washington's Implied Consent Law mean?
options: You must carry proof of insurance
By driving in Washington, you agree to be tested if an officer suspects you are impaired
You consent to vehicle inspections at any time
Passengers agree to wear seat belts
questions.correctAnswer: By driving in Washington, you agree to be tested if an officer suspects you are impaired
questions.explanation: Under the Implied Consent Law, everyone who drives in Washington agrees to be tested if an officer suspects they are under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

questions.question: If you refuse an impairment test in Washington, you could lose your driving privilege for:
options: 90 to 730 days, or until age 21 if that is longer
questions.correctAnswer: 90 to 730 days, or until age 21 if that is longer
questions.explanation: Refusing to be tested can cost you your driving privilege for 90 to 730 days, or until you reach 21, whichever is longer.

questions.question: What is Washington's minimum liability insurance for bodily injury or death of one person in a collision?
questions.explanation: Washington requires at least $25,000 for the bodily injury or death of 1 person in a collision.

questions.question: What is Washington's minimum liability insurance for damage to other people's property in one collision?
questions.explanation: Washington requires at least $10,000 for injury to or destruction of the property of others in any 1 collision.

questions.question: According to Washington's driver guide, tire tread should not be less than:
questions.explanation: The guide says tire tread shouldn't be less than 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When does Washington law require your headlights to be on?
options: Only when it is fully dark
From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise
From one hour after sunset to sunrise
questions.correctAnswer: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise
questions.explanation: Washington law says headlights must be on from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise.

questions.question: In Washington, when must you switch from high beams to regular headlights for an oncoming vehicle?
options: When you are 500 feet in front of it
Only if the other driver flashes their lights
questions.correctAnswer: When you are 500 feet in front of it
questions.explanation: Switch back to regular headlights when you are 500 feet in front of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: When following another vehicle in Washington, dim your high beams when you are within:
questions.explanation: Use regular headlights when you are within 300 feet behind another vehicle.

questions.question: Washington requires brake lights to be clearly visible from how far away?
questions.explanation: Brake lights are red and must be clearly visible from 100 feet away.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before turning or changing lanes in Washington?
questions.explanation: The guide says to signal 100 feet before you make your move.

questions.question: Under Washington's occupant protection rules, children up to what age must ride in a rear-facing car seat?
questions.explanation: Children up to age 2 must ride in a rear-facing car seat.

questions.question: In Washington, children aged 2 to 4 must ride in:
options: A car seat with a rear- or forward-facing harness
The front seat with an adult
questions.correctAnswer: A car seat with a rear- or forward-facing harness
questions.explanation: Children ages 2 to 4 must ride in a car seat with a rear- or forward-facing harness.

questions.question: In Washington, children 4 and older must use a car or booster seat until:
options: The vehicle's lap and shoulder belts fit properly — typically between ages 8 and 12
They are tall enough to see over the dashboard
questions.correctAnswer: The vehicle's lap and shoulder belts fit properly — typically between ages 8 and 12
questions.explanation: Children 4 and older ride in a car or booster seat until the lap and shoulder belts fit properly, typically between ages 8 and 12.

questions.question: What does an anti-lock braking system (ABS) do, according to Washington's driver guide?
options: It always shortens your stopping distance
It lets you keep better steering control but does not shorten stopping distance
It prevents skids on ice completely
It replaces the need for following distance
questions.correctAnswer: It lets you keep better steering control but does not shorten stopping distance
questions.explanation: An ABS does not shorten your stopping distance, but it allows you to keep better steering control.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck in Washington, what does it mean if you can't see the truck's mirrors?
options: The truck is about to turn
The truck driver can't see you
You are following at a safe distance
questions.correctAnswer: The truck driver can't see you
questions.explanation: If you can't see their mirrors, the driver can't see you.

questions.question: According to Washington's driver guide, how much cannabis is safe to use before driving?
options: Any amount if 8 hours have passed
questions.explanation: The guide states there is no safe amount of cannabis for driving.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, Washington's driver guide recommends you:
options: Open the window and keep going
Pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap
Drive faster to get home sooner
questions.correctAnswer: Pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap
questions.explanation: If you're tired, pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap.

questions.question: Under Washington's distracted driving rules, which is true about electronic devices?
options: You may hold a phone at red lights
You cannot hold any electronic device while driving
You may text if traffic is light
questions.correctAnswer: You cannot hold any electronic device while driving
questions.explanation: You cannot hold any electronic device while driving in Washington.

questions.question: How does Washington's driver guide classify road rage?
options: It is not addressed by law
questions.explanation: The guide states that road rage is a criminal offense.

questions.question: In Washington, who has the right-of-way at crosswalks and intersections?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians and bicyclists have the right-of-way at crosswalks and intersections.

questions.question: What should you do when a person with a service animal is crossing in front of you in Washington?
options: Don't honk — it's unlawful to interfere with a service animal
questions.correctAnswer: Don't honk — it's unlawful to interfere with a service animal
questions.explanation: It's unlawful to interfere with a service animal, and you should not honk.

questions.question: In Washington, what is the penalty for passing a stopped school bus?
options: There is no penalty if no children are visible
questions.explanation: Fines are doubled for anyone who passes a stopped school bus.

questions.question: On a school bus in Washington, what do red flashing lights mean?
options: The bus is about to move
questions.explanation: On school buses, red means stop and yellow means caution or slow down.

questions.question: In Washington, when must you yield to a transit bus?
options: When it has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway
Only at bus stops with shelters
questions.correctAnswer: When it has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway
questions.explanation: Yield to any transit vehicle that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway.

questions.question: According to Washington's driver guide, about how far does a loaded truck traveling 55 mph need to come to a complete stop?
questions.explanation: A loaded truck traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Before merging back in front of a large truck in Washington, you should:
options: See both of the truck's headlights in your rearview mirror
Honk to let the driver know
Speed up to 10 mph over the limit
questions.correctAnswer: See both of the truck's headlights in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Make sure you can clearly see both of the truck's headlights in your rearview mirror before merging in front of it.

questions.question: Under Washington's driver guide, may you share a lane with a motorcyclist?
options: Yes, if the lane is wide
No — never move into the same lane alongside a motorcyclist
questions.correctAnswer: No — never move into the same lane alongside a motorcyclist
questions.explanation: Never move into the same lane alongside a motorcyclist, even if the lane is wide.

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist in Washington, leave at least how much space?
questions.explanation: Leave at least 3 feet of space when passing a bicyclist.

questions.question: According to Washington's driver guide, how far can it take a train to come to a full stop?
questions.explanation: It can take up to a mile for a train to come to a full stop.

questions.question: When you must stop for a train in Washington, stop how far from the nearest rail?
questions.explanation: Stop between 15 and 50 feet away from the nearest rail.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way at a railroad crossing in Washington?
options: Vehicles, if the gate is up
questions.explanation: Trains always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: How can you identify a slow-moving agricultural vehicle in Washington?
options: A triangle sign or emblem on the back
A square yellow sign on the front
questions.correctAnswer: A triangle sign or emblem on the back
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display a triangle sign or emblem on the back.

questions.question: On Washington's knowledge test, how many correct answers do you need to pass?
questions.explanation: The Washington knowledge test is multiple choice; you must get 32 out of 40 correct to pass.
questions.sourceTitle: Do I need to take a test? — Washington State Department of Licensing
